business_problem: Baseten needed to serve frontier reasoning models across a global multi-cloud GPU fleet, but growing model sizes, long reasoning traces, and provider fragmentation forced painful tradeoffs between latency, throughput, and cost.
solution_summary: Baseten redesigned its serving platform around NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs on Google Cloud, NVIDIA Dynamo, NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, and CUDA so customers can scale large reasoning models without manually coordinating GPU islands. The company already pooled infrastructure from more than 10 cloud providers across dozens of regions, but Blackwell and its own multi-cloud capacity management layer let that fleet behave like a single elastic resource. Baseten provisions thousands of GPU instances, routes traffic to the best available region, and uses TensorRT-LLM plus Dynamo to keep large-context workloads such as DeepSeek-R1 and Llama 4 performant while reducing latency and cost. The move to Blackwell on A4 VMs and HGX B200 systems also gave Baseten enough memory bandwidth and interconnect speed to serve modern reasoning models in real time instead of forcing customers to choose between responsiveness and price-performance.

data_flow: Customer prompts are routed through Baseten's multi-cloud capacity manager to available Blackwell clusters, Dynamo and TensorRT-LLM optimize inference, CUDA-backed orchestration keeps GPU pools fungible across providers and regions, and the served outputs return to applications with lower latency and better cost efficiency.
business_outcome: Baseten increased throughput 5x for high-traffic endpoints, improved price-performance by up to 225% for DeepSeek-R1 and Llama 4 serving, and cut latency for large LLMs by up to 38%, letting customers deploy reasoning applications with faster responses and lower infrastructure spend.
